title: U.S. House · Alabama's 3rd Congressional District
area: East-central Alabama, including Anniston, Auburn, Opelika, and Phenix City along the Georgia border.

context.text: Incumbent Mike Rogers (R) defeated Terri LaPoint 83.2% to 16.8% in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary; Lee McInnis advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed. Cook Political Report rated the district R+23 for 2026.

candidates.name: Mike Rogers
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, 83.2% to 16.8%, over Terri LaPoint.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 3rd Congressional District (since 2003)

summary.text: Mike Rogers is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2002. He chairs the House Committee on Armed Services in the 119th Congress, having previously served as the committee's ranking member. He earlier served in the Alabama House of Representatives, including as minority leader.

background.text: Born in Hammond, Indiana, in 1958; earned a bachelor's degree in political science (1981) and a Master of Public Administration (1984), both from Jacksonville State University, and a J.D. from Birmingham School of Law (1991).
Served on the Calhoun County Commission from 1987 to 1990, then in the Alabama House of Representatives from 1994 to 2002, serving as minority leader from 1998 to 2000.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Armed Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served as Ranking Member of the House Committee on Armed Services in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).
Served as Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security in the 116th Congress (2019-2020).

candidates.researchNotes: Rogers has not completed a recent Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and his current campaign website did not list a distinct 2026 issues page as of the research date; priorities and issue positions were not found and are left blank rather than inferred.

candidates.name: Lee McInnis
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.

summary.text: Lee McInnis is a retired U.S. Army intelligence officer and the Democratic nominee for Alabama's 3rd Congressional District. He served nearly three decades in the Defense Intelligence Community, including overseas postings in Qatar, Bahrain, Iraq, and Afghanistan, and later taught at the college level.

background.text: Born in Birmingham and raised in Homewood, Alabama; graduated from Homewood High School and earned bachelor's (1983) and master's (1987) degrees from Auburn University, later returning to earn a second master's degree in history from Auburn in 2024.

Served in the U.S. Army from 1983 to 1989 as an Arabic linguist, then spent 28 years in the Defense Intelligence Community with postings in Qatar, Bahrain, Iraq, and Afghanistan, receiving the Joint Staff Civilian Commendation Medal and the Defense Intelligence Agency's Director Intelligence Medal.
Is affiliated with Indivisible Auburn/Opelika, the NAACP (Branch 5038), Auburn United Methodist Church, the National Eagle Scout Association, and the American Legion.

priorities.text: Health care: says Republican budget cuts to Medicaid and health spending threaten rural hospitals, citing an estimate that Alabama could lose 20 rural hospitals and 200,000 to 500,000 residents' health coverage.
priorities.quote: 83% of Alabama's rural hospitals are running at a financial loss.

priorities.text: Education: says he opposes what he calls a "two-tier" education system and supports revitalizing technical education and making college more affordable.
Economy and tariffs: says tariffs are raising prices and hurting farmers in the district, and that the economy should "lift all people."

positions.summary: Says GOP cuts to health spending will be "catastrophic" for rural Alabama hospitals and that a robust Veterans Health Care System is needed.
Says the ultra-rich and large corporations should pay a fair share of taxes, and that working and middle-class Americans have carried too much of the tax burden.
positions.quote: Make sure the ultra-rich and corporations pay their fair share.

positions.summary: Says tariffs are causing rising prices and job losses and hurting farmers in his district.
